adds.title: Policy 713: LGBT school policy change causes political turmoil in Canada
adds.summary: On 1 July 2023, changes to New Brunswick's Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity policy (Policy 713) took effect, barring teachers from using the preferred names and pronouns of students under 16 without parental consent and dropping explicit wording that let students take part in extracurricular activities, including sports teams, reflecting their gender identity. Premier Blaine Higgs's Progressive Conservative government updated the policy without a legislative vote, citing complaints from parents and teachers, and two ministers quit in protest while two others were pushed out. Party dissidents called for a leadership review and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said trans kids in New Brunswick 'need to feel safe, not targeted by politicians'. Documents the July 2023 amendment and political crisis this record describes.

adds.title: New Brunswick's proposed education policy change sparks backlash in Ottawa
adds.summary: Canadian Press via Global News (9 June 2023): the Higgs government's proposed Policy 713 changes would force children under 16 to get parental consent to change their names or pronouns at school, with the changes set to take effect 1 July 2023, reversing a three-year-old policy that required teachers to get the student's informed consent before discussing names and pronouns with parents. Eight Progressive Conservative members, including six cabinet ministers, sat out question period to protest the lack of process and transparency, and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said trans kids in New Brunswick 'need to feel safe, not targeted by politicians'. Confirms the under-16 parental-consent rule, the 1 July effective date, and the caucus revolt behind this record's 2023 amendment.

adds.title: 'We know it saves lives:' hundreds go to N.B. rally against review of LGBTQ policy
adds.summary: About 350 people rallied at the New Brunswick legislature on 14 May 2023 to protest the government's review of Policy 713, the 2020 policy that requires schools to respect students' chosen names and pronouns and provide gender-neutral bathrooms. Gail Costello of Pride in Education, who helped write the policy, said 'we know it saves lives' and warned that 'with this policy changed or removed, we're going to lose kids', while Education Minister Bill Hogan confirmed the review. Documents the public protest against the Higgs government's move to amend the sexual-orientation and gender-identity policy this record is about.

adds.title: Suman 46 homicidios LGBT+ en Michoacán entre 2015 y 2024
adds.summary: Quadratín Michoacán (16 May 2025) reports the Observatorio Nacional de Crímenes contra Personas LGBT count for the state: 46 LGBT+ homicides in Michoacán between 2015 and 2024, with Morelia highest at 11, followed by Lázaro Cárdenas (6), Apatzingán and Uruapan (5 each) and Zamora (4), and 2015 the deadliest year with 10 victims, presented at a press conference by Raúl Martínez of Colectivo Michoacán es Diversidad. Trans women were the most affected group (27 of the homicides) and people aged 25-39 the most affected age bracket, with 13 disappearances of LGBT+ people reported between 2022 and 2024. Matches the observatory counts cited in this record's summary.

adds.title: Concentran mujeres trans 58% de los asesinatos a personas LGBT+ en 2025
adds.summary: Quadratín Michoacán (16 June 2026) reports that trans women were 58.3% of LGBT+ homicide victims nationally in 2025 (35 of 60 recorded by the Observatorio Nacional de Crímenes de Odio contra Personas LGBT+), then gives the Michoacán picture: six homicide cases identified by civil-society groups in the state in 2026 (three in Morelia, one each in Uruapan, Ocampo and Maravatío) and at least 56 registered aggressions against the community since 2014, per Raúl Martínez, spokesperson of Colectivo Michoacán es Diversidad, speaking before the march for the transfeminicide of Daniela. Confirms the ongoing lethal violence against trans women in Michoacán that this record documents.

adds.title: Michoacán, sin atender a víctimas y sin reconocer violencia hacia la comunidad: Colectivo LGBT+
adds.summary: MiMorelia (11 June 2025) quotes Raúl Martínez of Colectivo Michoacán es Diversidad and the Observatorio Nacional de Crímenes de Odio contra Personas LGBT: of the 46 hate-crime cases recorded by civil society in Michoacán since 2015, only one was being processed for judicialization — the murder of Meredith Escarlet, a trans woman killed in Tarímbaro — while the state prosecutor's office keeps no disaggregated data. Martínez said Michoacán has stopped attending to victims and does not recognize the violence, that institutions such as the victims commission, the state human-rights commission and the state council against discrimination lack the capacity or budget to act, and that no public prevention policy exists. Documents the impunity and lack of institutional response central to this record's Michoacán assessment.

adds.title: The Reality of Transgender Welfare Boards in India: An RTI Investigation
adds.summary: The Quint (5 November 2024) publishes an RTI investigation into transgender welfare boards: West Bengal is one of the 12 states/UTs that notified a board, but the majority of boards have held fewer than one meeting per year since their creation, and the 17 existing boards 'are mostly running rudderless without a policy framework, compliance mechanism, or any power', with several functioning as non-transparent bodies that diffuse demands instead of serving trans people. Supports this record's claim that West Bengal's constituted welfare board operates without a functioning policy framework.

adds.title: Transwoman alleges RPF constable groped her to 'check gender'
adds.summary: Times of India, Kolkata (18 August 2024): a group of trans women heading to RG Kar Medical College filed an FIR alleging an RPF constable at Rabindra Sadan metro station groped one of them 'to check her gender' and made inappropriate remarks. Metro Railway and the RPF denied the allegations and counter-filed an FIR against the group, while footage showed the trans woman in tears. Documents the state-actor gender-checking conduct this record associates with West Bengal's policing of trans people.
